newsitem.title: CHINA: HK should hold free, fair elections soon - London.
newsitem.headline: HK should hold free, fair elections soon - London.

text.p: Hong Kong's new government should hold free and fair legislative elections as soon as possible, Britain's Foreign Office has said.

In its first six-monthly report on Hong Kong, covering the period from January to June 1997, Britain pledged vigilance to ensure that freedoms are maintained in its former colony, which it handed back to China at midnight on June 30 after 156 years.

The report, extracts of which were made available to the media by the British consulate in Hong Kong early on Thursday, said Britain had a strong responsibility towards making sure that Hong Kong's high degree of autonomy was preserved.
Hong Kong, now a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China, is promised a high degree of self rule under Sino-British treaties on Hong Kong's handover.

Just a month after the sovereignty change, however, Hong Kong's new administration has been battered by legal challenges against its China-appointed interim legislature, which supplanted an elected chamber at the handover.
New leader Tung Chee-hwa has promised to hold elections before mid-1998.

"The SAR government should hold free and fair elections as soon as possible to a new Legislative Council. Britain will take a close interest in the arrangements for the elections and the manner in which they are carried out," the statement from the Foreign Office said.

"Although Britain is no longer the sovereign power, the government has a deep and abiding commitment towards Hong Kong," it said, adding that such six-monthly reports will continue till at least the year 2000.

In reply, the Hong Kong government said in a statement that it was committed to making sure the territory maintained its high degree of autonomy, a pledge that China has repeatedly said it would abide by.
"The Central People's Government is equally committed, and this has publicly been reaffirmed by President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng," the Hong Kong government statement said.
